All rights reserved. @@ -285,0 +285,12 @@ + private static void checkDimensions(final int width, final int height) { + if (width <= 0 || height <= 0) { + throw new IllegalArgumentException( + "width " + width + " and height " + height + " must both be > 0"); + } + long lsz = (long)width * height; + if (lsz > Integer.MAX_VALUE) { + throw new IllegalArgumentException( + "width " + width + " * height " + height + " overflows int"); + } + } + @@ -289,0 +301,38 @@ + * @apiNote + * There are limits on the size of a {@code BufferedImage} that derive from + * the APIs involved and the exact implementation of a particular pre-defined type. + *
    + *
  • {@code BufferedImage} is an image type that supports {@link #getNumXTiles() only one tile}. + *
  • The organization of samples (e.g. red, green, blue, and alpha channels) for the pixels + * are specified by the {@code SampleModel}. + *
  • Each of the pre-defined image types documents the {@code SampleModel} subtypes + * that it can use, not always directly, but as required by the {@code ColorModel}. + *
  • {@code SampleModel} supports only supports up to {@code Integer.MAX_VALUE} pixels, + * so no {@code BufferedImage} can exceed that number of pixels. + *
  • The pixels are stored in a {@code DataBuffer}. + *
  • A {@code DataBuffer} is a container for one or more banks of + * Java primitive arrays so the number of data elements that can be + * stored per bank is limited by the maximum size of a Java array. + * This is at most {@code Integer.MAX_VALUE} elements, and may be less. + *
+ * Therefore, the number of data elements needed per pixel for an {@code imageType} + * further limits the maximum image size, and this is not the same for all pre-defined + * image types. + *

+ * For example {@code TYPE_3BYTE_BGR} uses byte array elements for storage. + * If the {@code ComponentSampleModel} used by the implementation supports + * only a single bank in its {@code DataBuffer}, then it will only be able + * to hold one third as many pixels as an implementation that uses a + * {@code BandedSampleModel} and a {@code DataBuffer} with 3 banks, one per band. + *

+ * And {@code TYPE_INT_BGR} needs only one bank in its {@code DataBuffer} + * to support the same image size as the banded 3 byte format. + *

+ * So the maximum number of pixels in a {@code BufferedImage} is + * format and implementation dependent. Applications must be aware of these + * limitations when creating images. + * @implNote + * This implementation uses a single data bank to store all image data for + * the pre-defined image types {@code TYPE_3BYTE_BGR}, {@code TYPE_4BYTE_BGR}, + * and {@code TYPE_4BYTE_ABGR}. + * @@ -292,0 +342,9 @@ + * @throws IllegalArgumentException if {@code width} or {@code height} is + * not greater than zero. + * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the multiplication product of + * {@code width} and {@code height} exceeds {@code Integer.MAX_VALUE}, + * or, when further multiplied by the number of data elements per pixel + * for the specified {@code imageType}, exceeds the maximum that can be stored + * by this implementation. + * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the {@code imageType} is not one of + * the pre-defined recognized image types. @@ -310,0 +369,25 @@ + + checkDimensions(width, height);
